additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.

subtypes.Self-Induced Vomiting: Intentionally inducing vomiting to remove ingested food.
subtypes.Misuse of Medications: Repetitively misusing laxatives, diuretics, or enemas for the purpose of weight control.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors (such as self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse, fasting, or excessive exercise) aimed at preventing weight gain. Self-evaluation is unduly influenced by body weight and shape, but individuals are typically within a normal or above-normal weight range, distinguishing it from classic presentations of anorexia nervosa. The disorder often emerges in adolescence or young adulthood but can present or recur later in life, frequently in the context of interpersonal stress, role changes, or weight-focused environments. The course may be chronic or episodic, with shame and secrecy often delaying help-seeking until medical complications, worsening mood, or functional impairment become difficult to hide.

patient.stressor: Lucy was promoted informally to a lead tech role when her shop started taking on more hybrid and EV work, which meant longer hours, heavier responsibility, and a younger crew looking to her as the example of what a "tough, no-nonsense" mechanic should be. As the workload grew and breaks became more rushed, she found herself grabbing quick, high-calorie meals between jobs and then feeling ashamed when she saw herself in the reflective glass of the service bay next to the slimmer younger techs and the fitness-focused customers. In an effort to "get back in shape" and prove she could keep up physically, she began swinging between eating large amounts of food after stressful shifts and then forcing herself to get rid of it so the weight "wouldn’t stick," a pattern that intensified over the last five months as the shop entered its busiest season. She finally agreed to see a psychiatrist after an embarrassing episode where she had to excuse herself repeatedly during a church potluck, and her pastor’s wife gently asked if she was okay because she seemed "worn down" and was disappearing to the restroom right after eating.
patient.chief_complaint: I’ve gotten into this habit of making myself throw up after I eat, and I can’t seem to stop doing it even though I know it’s not right.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: Any time the scale even creeps up half a pound or I catch a glimpse of my stomach sticking out a bit in the glass at the shop, I panic and start thinking, ‘I can’t let myself turn into some out-of-shape old lady,’ and it feels like I’ll do anything not to gain weight.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: These days I pretty much judge myself by what I see in the mirror at work—if my coveralls look tight or my face looks puffy next to the younger guys, I feel like a failure, like I don’t deserve this lead tech spot no matter how good I am with the cars.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.
S048.manifestation: After I eat, especially after a big meal or something greasy from the food truck, I’ll head straight to the bathroom and make myself throw up until I feel empty, and I’ve gotten so used to it that I plan my breaks and even church potlucks around when I can sneak off to do it without anyone noticing.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: On the nights when it’s been crazy busy in the shop and I finally get home, I’ll stand at the kitchen counter and just plow through half a pizza, a bag of chips, and whatever leftovers are in the fridge in like twenty minutes, way more than my husband or kids eat, even if I wasn’t all that hungry to start with.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start eating like that, it’s like a switch flips—my hands keep grabbing food and shoving it in my mouth even while my head is yelling, ‘Stop, you’re going to hate yourself for this,’ but I just can’t seem to slow down until I feel sick.

add_requirements.binges_and_compensatory_behaviors_freque: Pretty much every week since things picked up at the shop, there have been several nights where I binge when I get home and at least a couple of times I’ll force myself to throw up afterward, so it’s not just a once-in-a-while thing anymore.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: Lately I’ve been dragging at work and ducking out to the bathroom so much after grabbing food that my boss has asked if I’m sick, and I’ve started avoiding meals with my family or church because I’m embarrassed about how I eat and what I do after.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about five months now, pretty much since I took on the lead tech role and the shop got slammed with all the hybrid and EV work.
